html:
The Latji Latji are an Aboriginal Australian people of northwest Victoria, on the Murray River around today's Mildura. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their country is mallee scrub away from the river and red gum flats and lagoons along it, where fish and waterbirds were plentiful. Little is recorded of them in detail. Neighbours on the map include the Kureinji, the Dadi Dadi and the Wergaia. Pastoral runs took up the river frontage in the 1840s, and irrigation farming came to Mildura in the 1880s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
